newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady, liquidity low.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady, liquidity low.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady in Monday morning trade.
"Demand for kuna funds was quite high due to bank accounts thinning out as expected, following the payment of monthly tax by their clients on Friday," one dealer told Reuters.
She said some kuna funds were still on offer, but creditors and clients could not agree on terms.
Fresh loans totalled 29 million kuna ($4.8 million), most of which were call money borrowings struck at 10.5 percent. A single deal was made at 11 percent, loaned to a savings bank.
Term loans granted at 12, 15 and 16 percent accounted for some eight million kuna in fresh trade.

Weekend overnight trade totalled 27.4 million kuna sought by five banks with shortfalls. Another five banks wanted to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.001 Croatian Kuna)
